To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
acidification inactivates Ca2+ transport in sarcoplasmic vesicles.

the inactivation of calcium transport by acid in sarcoplasmic vesicles is due to protonation of an essential group in a site that is required for the conformational transition of ATPase to its calcium transport form.
acid inactivation of Ca-ATPase is accompanied by changes in the properties of the Ca-binding sites, and that the temperature dependence of the ATPase reaction is altered in the inactivated enzyme.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of acid pH (5.5-4.5) on the function and properties of the sarcoplasmic (Ca2+)-ATPiase system.
the role of calcium and magnesium ions in the regulation of muscle contraction and relaxation.
the mechanism of Ca2+ translocation by the sarcoplasmic Ca2+-ATPase.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
acid inactivation of (Ca2+ + Mg2+)-dependent ATPase and calcium uptake is a consequence of the protonation of a group with a pK of about 5.5.
the acid-induced inactivation of the calcium pump of sarcoplasmie reticulum is a specific inactivation which is not a consequence of the inactivation of the (Ca2+ + Mg2+)-dependent ATPase.

the acid inactivation of sarcoplasmc reticulum calcium uptake is due to a proton-induced conformational change which is not related to the ATP-dependent calcium transport mechanism but is closely associated with it, and which is not due to a simple denaturation or to the protonation of an essential group.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the acid inactivation of Ca transport in the SR is due to a protonation of a site on the Ca transport protein.
the proton is a powerful inhibitor of the calcium pump in skeletal muscle sarcoplasmic Reticulum.
acid inactivation of Ca uptake by sarcoplasm is a process which is reversible in that Ca uptake can be restored if the acid is removed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
acidification of the sarcoplasmic space is a powerful means of controlling calcium uptake.
the acid-induced inactivation of calcium transport in sarcoplasmic vesicles is not due to a direct effect on the ATPase.
the Ca2+-pump is inactivated by a proton attack on a sulfhydryl group, which is a common mechanism of inactivation for many enzymes.
